description: Han Feng raised to 3,000,000 with A ♠ A ♣ and took down the first pot at the final table.

Gagliano checked, Boos checked back and the pot was pushed to the Frenchman.

It folded around to Rami Hammoud in the small blind. "It's time to channel the spirit of Greg Raymer," he said, before putting on his sunglasses and shoving with J ♠ 5 ♣ . Evagoros Evagorou folded 9 ♦ 7 ♦ in the big blind. "Are they his sunglasses?" someone asked at the table. "They are! I reached out to Greg [Raymer]." said Hammoud. "I wanted to wear those sunglasses. So I said to him, 'I busted you, I wanted to pay respects. I couldn't find them.'" "And Greg replied that he had a couple if I want [some]."

Jamie Shaevel raised from early position to 4,000,000 and Evagoras Evagorou moved all-in for 23,000,000. The rest of the table folded and Shaevel called, covering Evagorou by five big blinds. Evagoras Evagorou: J ♠ J ♥ Jamie Shaevel: A ♥ Q ♦ The flop came 9 ♠ 7 ♦ A ♣ with Shaevel's top pair dominating Evagorou. The turn was a clean 5 ♠ for Shaevel, leaving Evagorou needing a jack on the river. He couldn't find it as the 4 ♣ completed the board. Evagorou bowed out in 9th place, banking $1,000,000. Speaking to Jeff Platt after his elimination, Evagorou said, "Overall, I am very happy. It was an amazing experience to reach the final table." "Now I am a little disappointed because I lost a flip but at end of the day I'm happy for what I achieved." "I am proud, but I prepared a long time for this. I'm happy for my achievement."

Jamie Shaevel raised to 10,000,000 with 4,500,000 behind. Lucas Jumalon asked how much he had back before calling. The flop came 7 ♠ 4 ♥ 3 ♣ and Jumalon checked. Shaevel put in his remaining chips and Jumalon thought briefly before calling. Jamie Shaevel: K ♥ 6 ♥ Lucas Jumalon: K ♦ 10 ♥ The turn was the J ♣ and the river the J ♥ sending Shaevel to the rail in seventh place as the first elimination on the second night's play. He takes home $1,500,000. "I'm definitely very emotional," Shaevel told Jeff Platt shortly after busting. "I'm sad right now, but also it won't take long for me to appreciate everything that's happened. It's been beyond a dream come true." "The sheer number of people who've flown from all four corners of the country, called, texted DM'd whatever - every possible method of telling me they're watching and rooting for me. I'm touched." Sporting a #8 Kobe Bryant jersey at the final table, Platt asked how much the 'Mamba Mentality' of the late NBA superstar influenced his play at the final table. "Growing up and watching Kobe and embracing and appreciating Mamba Mentality shaped who I am. The jersey I wore was given out at the memorial game after Kobe passed. It's very special to me, so I thought if I'm going down, I'd like to go down wearing this."

Jumalon found himself with an identical A ♠ 6 ♣ the very next hand and raised to 6,000,000. Once again, everyone else folded.

Lauri Saaskilahti raised to 6,000,000 from early position with 3 ♦ 3 ♣ . It folded to Rami Hammoud in the big blind with K ♥ 9 ♥ who shoved for 51,000,000. Saaskilahti folded his pocket pair.
Jumalon got a walk in the big blind.

Jumalon raised it to 7,000,000 with Q ♠ 4 ♣ in the small blind and Saaskilahti defended his big blind with 10 ♠ 8 ♦ . The flop was 2 ♣ A ♦ 2 ♥ and Jumalon added 3,000,000 to the pot. Saaskilahti folded.
Lucas Jumalon J ♣ 7 ♠ opened on the button to 6,000,000. Lauri Saaskilahti three-bet all in for 37,500,000 with 10 ♦ 9 ♦ from the small blind and got it through.
Han Feng raised to 6,000,000 with A ♣ 9 ♥ from under the gun and took down the pot.
"Push him the pot," said Greg Mueller, with Han Feng receiving a walk in the big blind.

Greg Mueller shoved from the button for 39,000,000 and was called by Rami Hammoud in the big blind. Greg Mueller: 9 ♠ 9 ♦ Rami Hammoud: A ♠ K ♥ The clean flop of 10 ♣ 7 ♥ 3 ♠ kept Mueller in the lead. The turn was the 5 ♣ and the 10 ♥ left Hammoud with just six big blinds and Mueller moved to third in chips as his rail erupted. "Could you imagine being on that rail right now, Ali?" Nick Schulman asked Ali Nejad in the commentary booth. "Not without a beer," quipped Nejad.
Lucas Jumalon got a walk in the big blind.

Jumalon made it 7,000,000 from the small blind with 6 ♠ 5 ♣ . Lauri Saaskilahti with A ♣ K ♠ in the big blind three-bet to 16,000,000 and Jumalon made the call. The flop of 9 ♣ 10 ♦ 7 ♥ saw a bet of 10,000,000 from Jumalon, Saaskilahti eyeballed his remaining stack of 30,000,000 but ultimately made the fold.

The broadcast resumed from the advertising break with Saaskilahti all-in on a Q ♥ Q ♦ 2 ♦ flop for 30,500,000. Han Feng was the only player along for the ride. Lauri Saaskilahti: K ♠ K ♥ Han Feng: A ♣ J ♦ The turn was the 3 ♠ and the river 9 ♥ secured the Finn a big double.
Luacs Jumalon raised to 6,000,000 with 7 ♣ 3 ♣ from the cutoff and took down the pot.

Rami Hammoud raised to 12,500,000 from under the gun leaving himself 4,000,000 behind. Lucas Jumalon called in the next position. The flop came 8 ♠ 6 ♠ 2 ♠ and Hammoud shoved for 4,000,000. Jumalon called. Rami Hammoud: Q ♥ J ♠ Lucas Jumalon: A ♥ 5 ♥ The turn was the 2 ♣ and the river was the 4 ♥ sending Hammoud to the rail in sixth place, taking home $1,750,000. Jumalon now sits with over 300 million in chips with five players remaining. Speaking to Jeff Platt afterwards, Hammoud said: "Grateful, a lot of gratitude... what an experience, to share this with all my friends and family, this will change my life." "Imposter syndrome is a big thing for me, to be able to see myself compete at the highest level... under the pressure this is massive for me." "And the money's pretty nice too, man! The money's pretty good!"

Greg Mueller on the button raised to 6,000,000 with Q ♣ J ♦ , Han Feng called with 10 ♥ 10 ♦ in the small blind, and Lucas Jumalon in the big blind with 7 ♠ 7 ♥ just made the call. The flop was A ♥ 7 ♦ A ♣ giving Jumalon sevens full. The chipleader and Feng both checked and Mueller made a bet of 3,000,000. Feng made the call and Jumalon raised to 18,000,000. Mueller got out of the way. Feng called and the dealer tabled the K ♠ turn card. Feng quickly checked and Jumalon tossed 15,500,000 into the pot and Feng made the call. The K ♦ river saw two quick checks and a huge pot was pushed the way of the runaway chipleader.
Han Feng raised to 6,000,000 from the button with J ♠ 10 ♦ . Lucas Jumalon three-bet to 64,000,000 with K ♦ 5 ♦ in the small blind. It folded back to Feng who also folded.
Short-stacked Michael Gagliano received a walk in the big blind.

Han Feng raised to 6,000,000 under the gun. Lauri Saaskilahti three-bet to 50,000,000 from the button. Greg Mueller picked up J ♦ J ♣ in the big blind. "Wow," said Mueller, removing his hat and sunglasses to deliberate. "50 [million]?" he asked Saaskilahti. "50," replied Saaskilahti. "Let's gamble." Mueller studied his stack and his opponents' stacks extensively and rubbed his face and head. "Do you want me to call?" Mueller asked Saaskilahti, receiving a quick telling off from the dealer. He laughed, and tanked some more, before ultimately folding. Feng called and was all in for 25,000,000. Han Feng: A ♦ A ♣ Lauri Saaskilahti: 9 ♠ 9 ♥ The 10 ♦ 8 ♦ 3 ♦ left Saaskilahti with only one nine to hit. However, the one out became seven with the J ♥ turn giving Saaskilahti an open-ended straight draw. Incredibly, the river was the Q ♠ and Saaskilahti made his straight to crack the aces and send Feng to the rail. "So brutal," said Nick Schulman on commentary. "Primordial screams and a barbaric end to Han Feng's Main Event," said Ali  Nejad. Speaking to the WSOP's Jeff Platt afterwards, referring to the nature of his exit Feng said, "It's fine, man, it happens. I'm all good." Platt then asked Feng about his future plans and he replied, "[EPT] Barcelona, it was already booked."

Lauri Saaskilahti under the gun raised to 6,000,000 and Lucas Jumalon called from the big blind. The flop came 9 ♠ 4 ♦ 2 ♥ . Jumalon led out for 10,000,000. Saaskilahti raised to 25,000,000 and Jumalon called. The 5 ♦ turn came and Jumalon bet 61,000,000 to give Saaskilahti a decision for his WSOP Main Event life. Saaskilahti looked at Jumalon and said "talk to me... if you have it, you have it," and made the call. Lauri Saaskilahti: 10 ♠ 10 ♣ Lucas Jumalon: 4 ♥ 3 ♦ The Finn only needed to survive the river card for an enormous double and he did so as the K ♦ was tabled, pushing the 188,500,000 pot to Saaskilahti.

Lucas Jumalon raised to 10,000,000 with 9 ♠ 5 ♠ in the small blind and Lauri Saaskilahti K ♥ J ♣ called in the big blind. The flop came A ♣ J ♥ 8 ♦ and Jumalon bet 5,500,000. Saaskilahti called. Both players checked the Q ♥ 7 ♠ runout and Saaskilahti took down the pot.
Lauri Saaskilahti shoved with 5 ♦ 3 ♣ in the small blind and Michael Gagliano folded J ♣ 7 ♦ in the big blind.
Lucas Jumalon raised to 7,500,000 with A ♠ 7 ♦ from under the gun and took down the pot.
Lauri Saaskilahti K ♦ 10 ♣ raised to 6,000,000 and took down the pot.

Lucas Jumalon 7 ♠ 6 ♥ limped in the small blind and Lauri Saaskilahti 9 ♦ 2 ♣ raised to 11,000,000 in the big blind. Jumalon called and the flop came A ♦ K ♥ 7 ♥ . It checked over to Saaskilahti who bet 6,000,000. Jumalon called once again and the turn was the Q ♥ . Both players checked and the river was the 4 ♥ . Jumalon bet 3,000,000 into a pot of 37,000,000 and Saaskilahti folded.
Lauri Saaskilahti raised to 6,000,000 with A ♦ Q ♣ in the small blind and took the blinds.

Lucas Jumalon raised to 6,000,000 with A ♠ 4 ♠ , Lauri Saaskilahti three-bet to 15,500,000 with A ♦ K ♥ and Jumalon called. The flop was J ♠ 8 ♣ 9 ♠ . Jumalon led for 13,000,000 and Saaskilahti made the fold.

Michael Gagliano shoved for 9,500,000 from the button. Greg Mueller called in the small blind with 4 ♥ 4 ♣ before Lucas Jumalon three-bet all in from the big blind. Mueller pulled a face and folded. Michael Gagliano: K ♠ Q ♠ Lucas Jumalon: K ♦ J ♥ "How you feeling Gags?" asked Jumalon. "Feel like I've felt since Day 6," replied Gagliano. "Let's see what happens." "A65 three diamonds?" said Jumalon. "A little greedy," replied Gagliano. "At least put ten-nine-something" The flop came K ♥ 8 ♥ 5 ♣ "Ace on the turn?" said Jumalon. "That's fair," said Gagliano. "No wait, why would...that wouldn't be fair." "For the chop? Let's chop up Greggy's money," said Jumalon. A J ♦ on the turn, however, removed the chance of a chop with Jumalon moving into the lead. The river was the 7 ♠ and Gagliano was eliminated in fourth place. "It's unbelievable," Gagliano told Jeff Platt. "I couldn't have asked for more. The support from my friends, my family, people online, people playing, the rest of the fans. It was just unbelievable. "Obviously, I wish I did a little bit more, but you do what you can with what you're dealt. I don't think I would have changed any decision at this final table. I was happy with how I played. Sometimes that's how it goes." "It's taken me a while to get there in poker. When I'm at the table, I'm just trying to make the best decision in that moment, in that spot, with the hands I've been dealt and the action that's happening. When I focus on that, I have my best results. "Obviously, I'd be lying if I said there were no nerves at all, but there are a lot of lights and cameras and everyone's really emotional, so I do my best to keep it level-headed, and I think I did a good job."
Greg Mueller moved all-in on the button with K ♦ 7 ♣ and got his bet through to take the blinds.

In the second hand of three-handed play, Lauri Saaskilahti limped in the small blind and Mueller checked in the big blind. The flop was 4 ♣ A ♦ A ♣ and both players checked. The J ♥ turn saw Saaskilahti bet 3,000,000 and Mueller called. After the 3 ♦ river, Saaskilahti asked for all of Mueller's chips and the Canadian obliged. Greg Mueller: 10 ♣ 4 ♥ Lauri Saaskilahti: K ♠ K ♦ Saaskilahti had successfully trapped Mueller to send him out of the Main Event in 3rd place with a $3,750,000 payday.
The opening hand was a quick one, as Lauri Saaskilahti raised to 9,000,000 on the button and Lucas Jumalon folded.
It was Jumalon's turn to raise on the button, making it 6,000,000. Saaskilahti folded and the stacks returned to where they began the night.

Lauri Saaskilahti raised to 9,000,000 on the button with J ♠ 10 ♣ , and Lucas Jumalon made the call holding K ♥ 4 ♦ in the big blind. Jumalon checked the 10 ♠ A ♥ 7 ♠ flop, and Saaskilahti continued for 6,000,000. That produced a fold from Jumalon.

Jumalon riased to 6,000,000 on the button with 10 ♣ 5 ♥ , finding a call from Saaskilahti with 7 ♣ 6 ♠ in the big blind. The 7 ♦ 9 ♠ 10 ♥ was checked by Saaskilahti, and Jumalon bet 10,000,000. The call was made, and another check from Saaskilahti followed the K ♠ turn. Jumalon slid out another bet, taking down the pot as Saaskilahti quickly folded.

Lauri Saaskilahti limped with 7 ♦ 4 ♠ on the button, Lucas Jumalon called with Q ♥ J ♥ . The flop was Q ♣ 5 ♥ A ♠ . Saaskilahti bet 3,000,000 and Jumalon called. The turn was the 6 ♣ , Jumalon checked and Saaskilahti led for 12,000,000. Jumalon called. The river was the 4 ♥ , giving Jumalon the checkmark. The chipleader checked, Saaskilahti checked back and Jumalon picked up the pot.

On the button, Jumalon picked up 8 ♠ 8 ♥ and limped. Saaskilahti checked his Q ♠ 5 ♦ . The dealer tabled a flop of 6 ♦ 8 ♣ 2 ♣ , giving Jumalon top set. Saaskilahti checked, Jumalon bet 4,000,000 and Saaskilahti called. The turn card was the 9 ♦ . Saaskilahti checked and Jumalon sized a bet of 30,000,000 into the existing 20,000,000 pot. Saaskilahti laid it down.
Saaskilahti looked down at A ♥ J ♥ on the button and raised to 12,000,000. Jumalon folded.
Lauri Saaskilahti looked down at A ♥ J ♥ on the button, raising to 12,000,000. Lucas Jumalon did not take long to let Q ♥ 6 ♠ go, and Saaskilahti took down the pot.

Jumalon raised to 8,000,000 on the button with 10 ♠ 2 ♥ , and Saaskilahti took some time with 10 ♣ 3 ♦ in the big blind before three-betting to 36,000,000. Jumalon folded, and Saaskilahti raked in the small pot.

Saaskilahti called on the button with Q ♠ 9 ♦ , and Jumalon checked his big blind option holding 10 ♠ 5 ♦ . Jumalon checked again on the 10 ♣ 7 ♥ A ♠ flop, and Saaskilahti bet 6,000,000. The call was made, and another check from Jumalon followed the K ♠ turn. Saaskilahti fired 22,000,000, and Jumalon slid in the call. The A ♣ river completed the board, and Jumalon checked one last time. Saaskilahti reached for chips, betting 37,000,000. Jumalon called with his two pair, aces and tens, and was correct to increase his chip lead.

Jumalon on the button looked down at Q ♠ 8 ♠ and limped. Saaskilahti with 10 ♥ 4 ♣ checked. The flop was 7 ♠ 8 ♦ A ♥ giving Jumalon middle pair. Saaskilahti checked and Jumalon checked back. The turn was the 2 ♥ to which Saaskilahti checked. Jumalon sized up a bet of 12,000,000, Saaskilahti exhaled and let it go.
Saaskilahti had 4 ♦ 3 ♦ on the button and raised to 12,000,000. Jumalon held 8 ♠ 8 ♦ and jammed. Saaskilahti insta-folded.

Jumalon with Q ♠ 6 ♠ on the button limped and Saaskilahti checked with J ♠ 3 ♣ . The flop of 8 ♦ 7 ♠ J ♥ gave Saaskilahti top pair and he opted to check. Jumalon checked back. The 10 ♥ turn saw Saaskilahti check and Jumalon bet 12,000,000. Saaskilahti called. The A ♠ river was quickly checked by the Finn and Jumalon checked back to see Saaskilahti pick up the pot.

Lauri Saaskilahti raised to 10,000,000 on the button, and Lucas Jumalon replied by moving all in from the big blind. This put Saaskilahti to a decision for his tournament life, and he took a moment while talking to his rail. "Let's go," said Saaskilahti as he made the call and the hands were turned up. Lauri Saaskilahti: A ♥ 10 ♦ Lucas Jumalon: A ♠ 9 ♣ The 4 ♠ Q ♦ A ♦ flop left Saaskilahti in good shape, but Jumalon spiked the 9 ♦ turn to sit one card away from the title. The room reacted as the 6 ♦ peeled off on the river, giving Saaskilahti a flush to earn the double and stay alive.

Lucas Jumalon limped with Q ♠ 5 ♦ on the button, and Lauri Saaskilahti checked holding J ♦ 3 ♦ in the big blind. Saaskilahti checked the 4 ♣ K ♠ A ♠ flop, and Jumalon continued for 4,000,000. The call was made, and another check from Saaskilahti followed the J ♠ turn. Jumalon fired twice the pot, betting 40,000,000. Saaskilahti called again to see the 6 ♠ river, checking once more. Jumalon took a moment before betting 180,000,000, sending Saaskilahti into the tank. "To hero or not to hero," Saaskilahti said aloud after taking a few minutes. "You have it?" Saaskilahti studied his opponent while Jumalon sat still. "I only have a jack," continued Saaskilahti. "It could be good." After taking some more time, Saaskilahti announced a call. Jumalon showed down his flush, sending his rail into a frenzy. That left Saaskilahti with less than 10 big blinds, as Jumalon regained a massive lead.

Lauri Saaskilahti looked down at A ♠ K ♠ and limped on the button. Lucas Jumalon with 6 ♦ 4 ♦ checked. The flop was A ♥ 9 ♦ 2 ♥ , putting Saaskilahti well in front. Jumalon checked and Saaskilahti sized up a bet of 4,000,000. Jumalon let it go.

Lucas Jumalon moved all in on the button, and Lauri Saaskilahti made the quick call in the big blind. Lauri Saaskilahti: A ♠ 7 ♦ Lucas Jumalon: K ♠ 6 ♦ Saaskilahti was ahead before Jumalon found a pair on the 6 ♠ 8 ♦ J ♠ flop. Jumalon then locked it up on the 6 ♣ turn, making trips to leave Saaskilahti drawing dead. The 4 ♦ river completed the board, as Saaskilahti had to settle for the runner-up spot.
